title: Bayesian demand hedging and credit ledger PRD (draft)
body:
Context and motivation:

Redwood Dedicated customers need predictable low-latency inference while the platform must make efficient use of constrained GPU capacity. Existing approaches (static reservations + naive burst crediting) either waste capacity during lulls or leave tenants exposed during spikes. This proposal combines probabilistic demand forecasting (Bayesian-style) with a transparent tenant credit ledger to create a ‘hedging’ layer: proactively reserve small soft buffers for tenants likely to spike, while enabling controlled borrowing and marketplace-style redistribution when spikes actually happen.

Goals
- Reduce user-facing 95th/99th latency spikes for Dedicated tenants without increasing overall reserved capacity by more than 7% on typical workloads.
- Provide tenant-level visibility and controls for soft-reserves, borrowing limits, and isolation fences.
- Minimize manual ops intervention; operator visible events should be exceptions, not routine.
- Ensure billing and cost allocation are auditable and simple to reason about.

Non-goals
- This PRD does not replace hard reserved capacity contracts or the SLA enforcement for critical tenants.
- Not aiming to migrate all autoscaling logic off cluster autoscaler; this is a higher-level policy/ledger that orchestrates existing scaling primitives.

High level design summary
The design has three cooperating components: (1) Bayesian Demand Hedger (BDH) forecast service, (2) Tenant Credit Ledger (TCL) with borrowing & settlement primitives, and (3) Brokered Isolation Controller (BIC) which enforces isolation semantics at runtime. Flow: BDH consumes telemetry (per-tenant QPS, token distributions, time-of-day, recent rollouts) and emits demand probability distributions and suggested soft-reserve sizes. TCL maintains per-tenant soft-reserve balances and a history of borrow events; it exposes APIs for allocate/borrow/repay. BIC couples with runtime to apply lane limits, preemptible reservations, and graceful degradation policies when borrowing limits are exceeded.

Key concepts
- Soft-reserve: a reserved headroom allocation recommended by BDH but not a hard contractual reservation. Soft-reserves can be preempted under operator policy but are intended to reduce cold-start/latency spikes.
- Borrow window: a bounded time window during which a tenant may borrow capacity beyond their hard reservation using credit. Borrowing is allowed only if TCL indicates available ledger credit or if operator policy permits emergency borrowing.
- Hedged buffer: probabilistic allocation sized to cover X% of predicted spikes (configurable per-tenant), e.g., 90th percentile over next 15 minutes.
- Isolation fences: lightweight runtime limits applied to prevent noisy neighbor amplification when a tenant borrows beyond allowed thresholds. Fences implement slow-down, partial response, or fallback routing to cheaper model variants.

Forecasting (BDH) details
- Inputs: per-tenant token-level telemetry, model variant mix, historical burst frequency, commit/CI tags (to flag deploy-driven traffic shifts), regional telemetry, and calendar features.
- Model: Bayesian hierarchical time-series (e.g., a lightweight probabilistic state-space model) that produces a short-horizon predictive distribution rather than a single point estimate. We prefer probabilistic outputs to set conservative soft-reserve sizes tied to percentile targets.
- Outputs: distribution summary (p10/p50/p90/p99), suggested soft-reserve size, confidence metric, anomaly flag.
- Refresh cadence: default 1 minute; adaptive to increased volatility (sub-minute if we detect a surge pattern).

Tenant Credit Ledger (TCL)
- Data model (surface-level): ledger entries are append-only records (allocate, borrow, repay, settle). Each tenant has: soft_reserve_allocated, credit_balance, borrowing_limit (configurable), last_settlement_ts.
- Credit sources: pre-purchased credits (enterprise addon), earned credits (good-faith buffer from underutilization), and ephemeral emergency credits (operator-controlled).
- Settlements: periodic settlement job reconciles actual borrow usage vs credits; invoices are generated for net consumption. We will include a rollup for transparency in the Console cost view.
- APIs: allocateSoftReserve(tenant, amount), borrowCapacity(tenant, amount, window), repayBorrow(tenant, amount), queryLedger(tenant, from_ts, to_ts).

Brokered Isolation Controller (BIC)
- Enforcement points: BIC integrates with serving runtime to apply: lane weights, soft preemption (graceful token draining), and fallback routing. On borrow events where TCL would be overdrafted, BIC will: 1) engage isolation fence for the tenant (reduce concurrency, lower batch size), 2) attempt to route excess to cheaper model variants or other regions, 3) if still unserved, return controlled 429/503 with clear error codes and recovery hints.
- Safety: all borrow-induced routing must preserve data locality/region constraints for tenants with private deployments. BIC will respect tenant isolation metadata.

APIs and UX
- Console: soft-reserve slider (percentile target + budget cap), borrow history view, projected cost impact preview, and a ‘simulate hedging’ mode to show expected latency improvements for different percentile targets.
- CLI/SDK: ledger APIs for programmatic allocation and custom borrowing strategies (e.g., CI-triggered temporary borrow on rollout).
- Alerts: when tenant borrow > 60% of their credit_balance or when BDH confidence drops below threshold while demand is rising.

Metrics and SLOs
- Tenant-facing SLO: reduce 99th tail latency during unplanned spikes by X% vs baseline (target value to be validated in sizing experiments).
- Platform metrics: soft_reserve_utilization, borrow_rate_per_tenant, overdraft_events, reconciliation_lag, forecast_confidence_distribution.
- Ops alerts: ledger reconciliation errors, anomalous forecast shifts (>3x within 5 minutes), and BIC preemption events frequency.

Billing and accounting
- Borrowing consumes credits; credits can be priced at a premium to discourage abuse. Early pilots will use a simple model: credits consumed are priced at 1.5x normal consumption rate.
- Clear, itemized statements per billing cycle showing soft-reserve allocations, borrows, repays, and net charge.

Operational considerations
- Backfill policy: when a tenant borrows and operates in another pool/region, router must tag requests for tracing and cost attribution.
- Auditing: append-only ledger with immutable IDs and settlement proofs; support export for compliance reviews.
- Rollback: feature gates for BDH and TCL to revert to baseline static allocation if needed.

Rollout plan (phased)
1) Internal-only pilot (2 tenants): enable BDH predictions + read-only ledger, surface suggestions in Console (no auto-allocate). 2) Controlled pilot (10 tenants): enable soft-reserve auto-allocation with conservative caps and manual operator override. 3) Public beta: enable borrowing with credit limits, expose billing previews. 4) GA: full automation, tiered pricing, and SLO guarantees.

Risks and mitigations
- Forecast miscalibration: enforce conservative caps initially and require human approvals for high confidence soft-reserve allocations. Retrain models frequently and monitor calibration metrics.
- Gaming/abuse: set borrowing pricing and automated throttles; offer audit trail and discretionary account limits.
- Complexity & observability: build clear Console surfaces and logs for each decision point; keep fallbacks simple and well-documented.

Open questions
- What percentile target should be the default for hedged buffers (90th? 95th?) — need experiment.
- How to map borrow events to downstream model licensing/costs for customers with special model entitlements?
- Pricing: premium multiplier testing — start with 1.5x and adjust based on elasticity.

Appendix: experiment plan
- A/B test: 50 pilot tenants split into control (static allocations) and treatment (BDH + soft-reserve at p90). Measure 95/99 latency, capacity utilization, and net cost delta over 30 days.
- Calibration test: simulate synthetic burst patterns (sawtooth, Poisson spikes) to tune BDH parameter priors.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally pragmatic: the forecasting model is lightweight and designed to be interpretable. The ledger is intentionally simple to avoid billing disagreements. Feedback requested on default percentile, pricing multiplier, and whether Console should allow auto-replenish of credits.

References: related PRDs and tickets are in linked_artifacts above.
